extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers; journalists and editors interested in wartime reporting
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting and dispatches covering wartime events, diplomatic statements, and domestic reactions from 1943; aimed at informing the public and guiding press behavior during war. Includes quotes from officials and reportage from multiple theaters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press vigilance against enemy propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: “He asked, ‘the press to be on guard against “the war of words, the lies and the false hopes” which will be spread from Berlin and Tokio.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: Harold Butler, British minister in Washington, warned in a speech that once Germany faces defeat it will attempt to weaken will and unity via propaganda. The remark is presented as guidance to the press to watch for and resist enemy disinformation during the war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding free speech and a free press as a war aim
rubrics_metrics.description: “Safeguarding of free speech and a free press must not only be a war aim ... the peace following the war will not have as its chief object the redetermination of geographical boundaries.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: Remarks (at a conference/dinner) emphasizing that protecting free speech and a free press should be part of the Allies' war objectives and part of postwar aims beyond territorial adjustments; implies an editorial/policy principle for press and policymakers.
